body: Unreal Championship 2: The Liandri Conflict is Epic Games' Xbox arena shooter, first released in North America on 18 April 2005. It takes the Unreal series' fast competitive battles and gives melee weapons a central place beside firearms. Switching to a blade or staff changes the view to third person, making the character's movement easier to read at close range. The result is a contest between distances as well as weapons. An opponent across the room and one about to strike demand different responses from the same player.

Characters belong to light, medium or heavy classes, with different balances of health, speed and striking power. A quick fighter can approach an encounter differently from a slower, stronger one, making movement part of the initial choice. Adrenaline abilities offer further ways to alter a confrontation. Firearms can be used from first- or third-person views, while close combat rewards attention to the opponent's position. The player learns when to keep firing, when to close the gap and when to escape before an enemy's advantage becomes decisive.

The game was designed around Xbox Live competition, with additional characters and content released through the service. Its modes include familiar arena objectives alongside variations such as Overdose and Nali Slaughter. Kevin Riepl composed the score, while Midway published the release. The combination of acrobatic movement, character differences and melee combat gave this sequel a particular identity within Unreal. Rather than simply reproducing the PC tournament format, it used the console setting to rearrange the relationship between the fighter on screen, the camera and the next attack.
